evidence_policy: Official patch mechanics only. Community build rankings require a separate real-game validation pass before promotion.

early.notes: 4.4 AI and colony systems favor designated, specialized worlds. Small empires expand more aggressively, while excessive undeveloped colonies are discouraged.

mid.notes: 4.4 raises AI ascension-path weighting and improves designation-matched building and zone planning.

late.notes: 4.4 shifts native AI endgame planning toward higher research targets and lower alloy ceilings.

core_mechanics: Arkships are mobile capitals, colonies, shipyards, and warships.
Waystations harvest systems without claiming them; adjacent stations form Waylines.
Contracts provide military, science, resource, and diplomacy objectives.
Nomadic empires may settle or settled empires may embark after the required tradition.
operational_rules: Do not use ordinary expansion logic for Nomadic empires.
Treat BUILD_STARBASE as Waystation-network intent when native AI supports it.
Treat COLONIZE as settlement intent only when the save explicitly reports settlement availability.
Prioritize Operational Reserves before optional spending; the critical stage penalizes research, unity, alloys, and job efficiency.

diplomacy_rules: Non-primary war participants can negotiate to join or leave ongoing wars.
A fully occupied empire accumulates escalating war exhaustion and attrition.
meta_rules_domestic: 4.4.6 CONFIRMED: specialize colonies to their designation, value unity and ascension paths, and avoid overextending into too many undeveloped colonies. NOMADS: manage Operational Reserves, Arkships, Waystations, Waylines, and Contracts instead of normal territorial expansion.
meta_rules_military: 4.4.6 CONFIRMED: use native AI specialization and preserve fog-of-war. Evaluate joining or leaving ongoing wars from known occupation, exhaustion, and diplomatic information. Weapon and fleet rankings require separate 4.4 gameplay validation.
